correctness.rationale: Reassessed complete replacement repairs/1/RESULT.md; no change to the mass theorem, transition rule or supporting checks. The original Limitations wrongly suggested fixed-generation counts need not inherit the componentwise mass order even while noting fixed classwise rescaling. The replacement states exactly when count conversion is valid: c_j=2^j x_j/m_0 for a common generation-zero mass m_0, so a positive diagonal map preserves the ordering and its converse; variable particle mass within a bin is outside that inference. For the final mass theorem, direct expansion cancels the p q term, leaving (p-q)D(BD-DB), whose only possibly nonzero entries are (p-q)s_(j+1)(s_j-s_(j+1)) on the first subdiagonal including the transition into the cap. For p>q, T(p)T(q) means q then p. Every earlier and later transition product is nonnegative, so adjacent swaps give simultaneous sorted maximality under the indicated survival ordering. Each wrong-sign coefficient is detected by the same two rates acting on e_j; strict positivity of s_(j+1) is needed for necessity. This verifies both iff orientations, mixed rises/falls, constant survival, ties and p=0 or 1. The exact sample vectors match direct two-step substitution. Frozen checker and verification notes were inspected, not executed; neither needs replacement.

value.rationale: For a natural finite cascade with stationary selective loss, the result answers when one schedule optimizes all retained bins simultaneously, and when no sorted orientation can be universally recommended. The two-step witnesses and the reversible sign criterion make this an exact structural classification, stronger than a scalar total-mass recommendation. It is valuable for the model, not advertised as calibrated marine management guidance; the count correction removes an inconsistency without changing that contribution.
